description: We are a team of six enthusiastic and passionate students interested in technology, innovation, and problem-solving. Our team enjoys exploring new ideas, learning new technologies, and building creative solutions to real-world problems. We believe in teamwork, collaboration, and sharing knowledge. We are looking to connect with motivated individuals who have skills in programming, web development and creative problem-solving. Together, we aim to learn, innovate, and build something impactful!
summary:
Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive platform that transforms Earth science information into dynamic audio experiences through data sonification. Developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project explores a new way to understand our planet by combining Earth observation, interactive visualization, and sound.

The platform aims to connect scientific data with meaningful audio patterns, allowing users to explore environmental changes through both visual and auditory experiences. By translating variations in Earth data into sound, it offers an alternative way to experience scientific information, particularly for people who are blind or have low vision.

Users can explore Earth through interactive 3D visualizations, satellite imagery, environmental datasets, and synchronized audio experiences. Our goal is to make complex Earth science more engaging, understandable, and accessible.

Earth Information Jukebox brings together science, technology, music, and accessibility to help everyone experience our changing planet in a different way.
details:
Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive web-based platform designed to transform Earth science information into sound-based experiences. The project addresses the challenge of making Earth observation data more accessible, engaging, and understandable through data sonification.

The platform combines interactive Earth visualization, satellite imagery, environmental information, and audio technologies. Users can explore geographical locations, interact with Earth visualizations, examine environmental information, and experience how changes in scientific data can be represented through sound.

The central concept is data sonification. Scientific measurements can be mapped to musical parameters such as pitch, rhythm, intensity, and frequency. This creates an auditory representation of environmental patterns, offering another way to interpret information beyond traditional maps and charts.

Accessibility is a major consideration. The project aims to support people who are blind or have low vision by providing auditory ways to explore Earth science information. It also aims to make scientific exploration more interactive for students, educators, and the general public.

The project uses modern web development technologies and interactive visualization and audio tools. NASA Earth observation resources are used where integrated into the application. Additional technologies and external datasets are documented in the project resource list.

The creative aspect of this project is the connection between Earth science and music. Instead of treating scientific information only as numbers or visual representations, Earth Information Jukebox explores how our planet's changing systems can become meaningful auditory experiences.

Our intended impact is to encourage inclusive scientific exploration and demonstrate how technology, creativity, and accessibility can work together to help people experience and understand our planet.
